title: GERMAN LANGUAGE – LEVEL 05
overview: German Language – Level 05 consolidates upper-intermediate communication through nuanced discussion, complex sentence patterns, critical reading, extended listening, and professional writing. Learners develop greater fluency and independence when evaluating evidence, handling unfamiliar situations, presenting arguments, and collaborating in German-speaking environments. The course integrates accuracy, appropriate register, intercultural awareness, and purposeful communication across authentic-style tasks.
audience: Learners who have completed German Language – Level 04 or possess comparable intermediate proficiency.
Professionals who need to participate in detailed discussions, meetings, presentations, and written exchanges in German.
Students and independent learners preparing for more demanding academic, social, or workplace language tasks.
methodology: Task-based language workshops combining grammar refinement with practical speaking and writing.
Structured discussions, case studies, simulations, peer feedback, and problem-solving activities.
Guided analysis of authentic-style articles, interviews, reports, and presentations.
Iterative drafting of professional texts, argumentation, and concise summaries.
Diagnostic practice, formative assessment, and a final integrated performance task.
competencies: Express and defend detailed viewpoints with coherent arguments and appropriate nuance.
Use a broad range of complex grammatical structures with increasing consistency.
Interpret extended speech and written texts, distinguishing evidence, tone, and implied meaning.
Produce clear, organized professional correspondence, summaries, and reports.
Manage discussions, presentations, negotiations, and intercultural exchanges independently.
objectives: Build coherent arguments using contrast, concession, condition, and consequence.
Apply advanced relative structures, passive alternatives, nominalization, and reported speech in context.
Evaluate information from articles, interviews, and workplace documentation.
Adapt register, tone, and communication strategies to different audiences.
Write structured reports, persuasive emails, and well-supported opinion texts.
Deliver and defend a presentation while responding constructively to questions.

items.text: Review complex clauses, case usage, tense choices, and formal registers.
Assess fluency, listening accuracy, reading strategies, and written organization.

Develop claims with examples, qualifications, and counterarguments.

outline.title: Reported Speech and Konjunktiv I Awareness

Rewrite complex formulations into clearer spoken explanations.
Refine verb–preposition combinations and case selection.
Use pronominal adverbs and complex reference structures.
Correct recurring errors through contextual editing.
Build natural verb–noun combinations and common fixed expressions.
Analyze compounds, prefixes, and derivational patterns.
Select vocabulary appropriate to professional and social contexts.
Follow extended interviews with differing viewpoints.
Identify speaker attitude, supporting details, and implied meaning.
Take structured notes and synthesize key points.

Adapt phrasing to professional hierarchies and intercultural settings.
Improve sentence stress, rhythm, and connected speech.
Practice pacing, emphasis, and intonation in extended explanations.

Research and synthesize information on a selected practical issue.
